irmaa._basis: Tax year 2024 MAGI determines the 2026 surcharge; tax year 2023 is used when the 2024 return is unavailable. partB is the TOTAL monthly Part B premium at that tier, not the surcharge alone.

_conflict.disagreement: The CMS 2026 fact sheet and SSA POMS HI 01101.031 both state $391,000. Federal Register 90 FR 52063 Section IV.C renders the same two dollar premiums against a $500,000 breakpoint. No CMS correction notice was found.
_conflict.resolution: Coded at 391000 on two-source agreement, including the SSA source that administers the determination. Confirm against the official Federal Register PDF before any client-facing use.

partD._note: There is no separate dollar initial coverage limit for CY 2026; the initial coverage phase ends at the $2,100 out-of-pocket threshold.

announced2027._note: CMS will discontinue the Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration at the end of CY 2026. The 2027 deductible and out-of-pocket threshold were not published as of 2026-10-27.

partB.duration: Charged for as long as the person has Part B. medicare.gov states 'usually charged for as long as you have that type of coverage'; the statute ties the increase to a continuous period of eligibility ending at death. The lifelong reading is an inference from Sec. 1839(d), not express text.
partB.excludedMonths: Months inside the Initial Enrollment Period, months before age 65, months covered by an employer group health plan based on current employment, months under State buy-in, and enrollment during the Exceptional Conditions Special Enrollment Period.

partD.formula: 1% x national base beneficiary premium x number of full months without Part D or creditable coverage
partD.trigger: 63 or more days in a row without Part D or other creditable drug coverage after the Initial Enrollment Period ends
partD.duration: Paid for as long as the person has Medicare drug coverage, including after switching plans or joining a zero-premium plan. The amount changes as the base beneficiary premium changes.

enrollment.initialEnrollmentPeriod: Begins three months before the month of the 65th birthday and ends three months after it.
enrollment.generalEnrollmentPeriod: January 1 through March 31 each year; coverage starts the month after sign-up.
specialEnrollmentPeriods: Own or spouse's job-based coverage: 8 months after work stops, or from when the coverage ends if that comes first.
Employer with fewer than 20 employees: any time while still working, or within 8 months after work stops or job coverage ends, whichever is first.
Family member's job-based coverage at an employer with 100 or more employees: 8 months after that family member stops working.
TRICARE tied to an active duty service member: 8 months after the service member retires.
enrollment.underSixtyFivePathways: Twenty-four months of Social Security or Railroad Retirement Board disability benefits, or immediately on benefit start for a person who has ALS.
